chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Abd al-Aziz al-Ubaydi from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Whoever says in his day, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He is One, without partner, the One God, the Eternal, who has neither a companion nor a child,' Allah will record for him forty-five million good deeds, erase from him forty-five million sins, raise him forty-five million levels, and it will be as if he has recited the Qur'an twelve times in one day, and a house will be built for him in Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah' with specific attributes?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the profound efficacy of a specific, elaborated formulation of Tawhid that underscores God's absolute oneness, indivisibility, and self-sufficiency (Al-Samad). The hadith quantifies the reward in millions of good deeds and sins erased, equating the spiritual merit to reciting the entire Qur'an twelve times, thereby highlighting the centrality of correct creed in Shia devotional practice. This immense reward reflects the Shia scholarly view that precise articulation of divine attributes carries weight comparable to the recitation of the Divine Word itself.
